resources.string: Turn your phone into a private local hub for TV, laptop, phone, tablet, and browser access.
Open your videos, photos, music, and files instantly on nearby devices without uploading them anywhere first.
Open on TV, laptop, iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, Android, or any other device with a browser.
The receiving device only needs your local link or QR code. No extra app is required on the other device.
Send files out, let people receive them, and collect files back from connected devices during the same session.
Everything works over the same Wi-Fi network or your phone hotspot, so local sharing stays fast and reliable.
Your data stays on your device with no cloud upload, no account, and no remote internet access in this build.

DirectServe lets nearby devices open your shared files in a browser without needing cloud storage or an account.
It is platform-independent for receivers, so any device with Wi-Fi or hotspot access and a browser can connect.
No cloud. No account. No internet required.
Share videos, photos, music, documents, and folders from your phone.
Open the session in a browser on Android phones, iPhone, iPad, Windows laptops, Mac, Linux, tablets, desktops, and many smart TVs.
Any device with Wi-Fi or hotspot access and a browser can connect on the same local network.
Keep one share open while several devices browse at the same time.
Most videos can play directly in the browser.
Some videos need a temporary browser-ready version for smoother playback on certain devices.
The original file stays on your phone, and playback preparation does not replace your source file.
Browser preparation is optional and mainly helps videos that need conversion open faster in some browsers.
You can start preparation when you want it, stop it any time, and keep watching while it runs.
Larger batches can take longer and may warm the phone a little, so it is best used only when needed.
Other devices can send files to your phone through the web view when uploads are allowed.
If upload approval is turned on, you will see a request before the files are accepted.
Received files are saved on your device and can appear in your history.
On the browser upload page, people can drag files into the drop zone to send them to your phone.
They can also choose files manually if drag and drop is not available on that browser.
Uploads stay inside your active local session and save into the device Downloads area.
More than one device can connect to the same session.
The live session screen shows connected devices, activity, and the generated device names with IP addresses.
You can block devices, disconnect everyone, or protect the session with a PIN.
DirectServe does not require an account and does not move your library into cloud storage.
Nearby devices only see the files and folders that are part of your current live session.
You can stop sharing, turn on a PIN, block devices, disable downloads, or stop browser preparation whenever you want.
Both devices should be on the same Wi-Fi network or your phone hotspot.
Public Wi-Fi sometimes blocks local device-to-device traffic, so hotspot is often the best fallback.
If downloads are disabled in Settings, the web UI hides download actions completely.
